The Physics of Exercise  

Dumbbells are clever tools because gravity provides constant resistance, but unlike barbells, they let you alter the lever arm to change intensity. When you squat holding one weight close to your chest, you shorten your moment arm, lowering torque on the knees and making the lift safer. On the other hand, extending your arms in a lateral raise increases torque, forcing the shoulder muscles to work harder even with a lighter load. This mechanical variability allows a 10 kg dumbbell to challenge multiple muscle groups effectively.

I remember a study from the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research showing that participants who manipulated the lever arm during dumbbell rows saw greater activation of the mid-trapezius than those using fixed-position bands. The lesson: small tweaks in positioning can transform a light weight into a serious stimulus.
